sections.heading: Materiality of the rating system and ongoing compliance
sections.text: The rating system is classified as material in the Bank's IRB rating system materiality assessment (share of IRB RWEA 1.3%, above the 1% threshold), which was communicated to the ECB in the annual IRB overview of April 2027 and is reviewed annually. The Bank maintains the documentation and evidence of continued compliance of the rating system with the IRB requirements in the model inventory and the self-assessment, to support the ECB's regular review. The rating system's exposures are included in the Bank's annual supervisory benchmarking submissions under CRD Article 78 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2070, prepared by Capital Reporting with an explanation of the methodologies; in the 2026 exercise the CCF-based EAD of the Bank was within the interquartile range of peers, so no divergence analysis was requested.

sections.heading: Governance and management reporting of the rating system
sections.text: The credit risk control unit for this rating system is Retail Credit Risk Modelling within Credit Risk Management, which is independent of Retail Banking (origination and renewal of credit), reports to the CRO and is responsible for the design, implementation, oversight and performance of the rating system, including participation in its validation and ongoing review. Quarterly management reporting to the Retail Credit Committee and semi-annual reporting to the Group Risk Committee cover the EAD and CCF per pool, migration of facilities between pools, the comparison of realised and estimated CCFs, stress test outcomes and the rating system's materiality, strengths, limitations and validation status. Senior management (the CRO and the Director Retail Credit Risk) is informed of material changes and exceptions and informs the Management Board; the post-model adjustment and the remediation plan were reported to the Management Board on 17 December 2024. Internal Audit reviews the retail IRB rating systems at least annually; the 2026 audit IA-2026-RCR-05 covered the CCF estimation and the remediation plan and had no high findings.

deficiencies.rationale: MDD section 6.2 sets MoC A-02 for the reconstructed overdraft limits at 1.2 percentage points, equal to the adverse effect of the two reconstruction rules tested by the developers. Model Validation's own sensitivity analysis with a third plausible rule (limit set to the maximum observed balance in the six months before migration) gives an adverse effect of 1.9 percentage points on the LRA of OD-1 and OD-2, so the applied MoC is lower than the plausible range indicates and no justification for the lower value has been approved by MRM.

mitigation.text: Extend the sensitivity analysis for A-02 to all plausible limit reconstruction rules, set the MoC at least at the most adverse plausible effect (1.9 percentage points for OD-1 and OD-2) or document an MRM-approved justification, and update the MoC register and MDD chapter 6.

deficiencies.rationale: The downturn report uses the 20-year time-span 2006–2026 and extends GDP and unemployment back to 1995 only 'for information'; it does not assess whether the variability of each indicator over the 20 years is representative of its likely future range, nor conclude whether an extension of the time-span is required.

mitigation.text: Add to the downturn report an assessment per indicator of the representativeness of the 20-year variability (for example comparison of standard deviation and extremes with the longer series) and document the conclusion on extending the time-span.

deficiencies.rationale: MDD section 7.6 concludes qualitatively that climate-related and environmental risks are not material for retail revolving CCFs, without a quantitative analysis or a reference to evidence on how physical or transition events affected drawings.

mitigation.text: Perform a quantitative materiality analysis (for example realised CCFs of obligors in areas affected by the 2021 Limburg floods and energy-price sensitivity of drawings in 2022) in the first annual review of estimates and document the outcome in MDD section 7.6.

deficiencies.rationale: The RDS documentation describes the three default-definition regimes P1–P3, but does not reference the register of current and past default definitions with approving body, approval and implementation dates and, for the IRB change of 2020, the change category and supervisory dates.

mitigation.text: Reference the CR-STD-110 default definition register in RDS section 3.3.4 and add the approval, implementation and supervisory notification dates of each regime.

deficiencies.rationale: The documents show a reconciliation of the RDS default flag with the production default register, but no quarterly reconciliation of the default flags used for IRB and IFRS 9 between the risk and finance systems for the retail revolving portfolio; the field stage3_ifrs9 is stored but not reconciled with dflt_irb.

mitigation.text: Until the quarterly IRB–IFRS 9 default flag reconciliation for cards and overdrafts is implemented by Finance and Credit Risk Management (target Q4 2027), perform a one-off reconciliation for the reference dates 2025–2026 and report differences in the annual review.

codeFacts.check: Utilisation band boundaries used for the LRA CCF per pool in the estimation code
codeFacts.detail: estimation/lra.py L57: UTIL_BANDS = [0.30, 0.70, 0.90] used to aggregate realised CCFs per pool (documented in MDD 4.4 and IS-CCF-REV-3.0: 30% / 70% / 95%; the scoring module scoring/pools.py L22 uses 0.95), so the published LRAs of CC-3/CC-4 and OD-3/OD-4 were estimated on a different pool definition than the one implemented.

One-sided t-test of realised versus estimated CCF per pool on 2024–2025 defaults: 9 of 10 pools green; OD-4 amber (realised 92.9%, best estimate 91.2%, p = 0.031 with MV's pool definition).
